thread:
Incident Bot: Paging *on-call* - high p99 latency detected for customer Cerulean (VPC, eu-west-1). Alert: p99 > 18s, p95 > 4.5s across dedicated pool cerulean-prod-eu.
Maya Ops: seeing the same in console, spike started ~2134566700. customer reports slow responses, their frontend has retries piling up.
Sam I.: acknowledged, I'm on it. Can someone grab tenant isolation check?
Leila (oncall): I'll take tenant isolation. Initial hypothesis: one tenant's batch job saturating KV cache and GPU pool. Running quick query.
Jordan P.: FYI autoscale didn't add nodes earlier due to quota error - saw a rollup in logs. Might need manual bump while we look.
Maya Ops: logs (snippet):
```
[2026-03-15T09:21:30Z] cerulean-prod-eu pool=cerulean-prod-eu nodes=6 qlen=1200 p50=120ms p95=6.2s p99=18.7s
[2026-03-15T09:22:02Z] autoscaler: scale_attempt=1 reason=quota_exceeded region=eu-west-1
[2026-03-15T09:22:05Z] tenant:tenant-cerulean-42 tokens/sec=9800 kv_hits_drop=0.2
```
Sam I.: beam me the full tenant list and top token rates. Also check if model variant rwd-xl-int8 was in use for Cerulean — sometimes bigger models blow up latency under burst traffic.
Leila (oncall): pulling per-tenant rates now. It looks like `tenant-cerulean-42` is at 60% of pool QPS, and two other tenants normally <5% jumped to 20%.
Carla CSM: pinging Cerulean ops contact (ftw). They say they kicked off a scheduled large batch at 09:15 UTC but shouldn't have hit prod inference - investigating.
Jordan P.: mitigation options: 1) shard traffic off to a warm spare in eu-central (route policy change), 2) manually scale the dedicated pool up + add an emergency burst pool, 3) apply per-tenant throttle for tenant-cerulean-42 via rate-limiter. I'd do 1+3 short term.
Maya Ops: +1 to routing to spare region. low-risk if we route read-only inference; need to confirm latency tradeoff for Cerulean's clients.
Leila (oncall): I'm starting tenant throttle for tenant-cerulean-42: `rwctl tenant throttle --tenant tenant-cerulean-42 --qps 1200 --reason "emergency mitigation"`
Leila (oncall): throttle command output:
```
Started throttle for tenant-cerulean-42: target_qps=1200 previous_qps=9800
Applied at 2026-03-15T09:24:12Z by leila_oncall
Expected impact: reduce burst load to pool by ~75%
```
Sam I.: applying route policy change to shift 40% of Cerulean traffic to eu-central warm spare: `rwctl route update --customer cerulean --split 60/40 --regions eu-west-1,eu-central-1`
Sam I.: route update acknowledged by deploy bot.
Incident Bot: Route change completed (deployment id: deploy-cerulean-2134568050).
Maya Ops: watching metrics... p99 dropped from 18.7s -> 9.3s after throttle + routing. p95 down to ~2.1s. Good signal.
Jordan P.: still seeing KV cache thrashing on pool nodes - recommend temporary increase of shared KV size and reduce model kv retention to free memory: `rwctl pool edit cerulean-prod-eu --kv-size 1.5x --kv-ttl 60s`
Leila (oncall): applied pool edits.
Leila (oncall): quick check: autoscaler quota still blocking full-scale so we coordinated with infra to request emergency quota bump. Infra ticket #INF-8759.
Carla CSM: Cerulean confirmed they halted the batch on their side. They want a post-mortem and a note on allowed batch sizes / recommended patterns. I'll coordinate with SE.
Sam I.: OK let's document short-term fixes and next steps in incident doc. Current state: degraded -> improving. Continuing to monitor for 30m.
Maya Ops: added temporary alert rule to notify if p99 creeps above 6s again for this pool.
Jordan P.: starting controlled rollback of throttles in 15m, but keep route split until traffic normalizes.
Leila (oncall): handoff to Sam for the 2nd shift (Sam you own watch at 10:15 UTC). Sam will escalate to Eng Infra if autoscaler quota isn't fixed by then.
Sam I.: taking handoff. Noted actions: 1) keep route split 60/40, 2) monitor p95/p99 and KV metrics, 3) confirm quota resolution INF-8759, 4) draft follow-up with Cerulean SE and CSM.
Incident Bot: On-call Handoff recorded: from Leila (oncall) -> Sam I. at 2026-03-15T10:15:00Z
Maya Ops: final note before handoff: no errors from model runtime, latency was purely resource saturation. Also flagged: consider adding per-tenant soft limits to Dedicated pools for enterprise customers to avoid future blast radius.
Carla CSM: I'll schedule a customer call and include mitigations + recommended config (warm spare routing + per-tenant thresholds).
Sam I.: will keep thread open for updates. If anyone sees p99 > 6s re-alert here.
Leila (oncall): thanks all — nice quick collaboration. :raised_hands:
Sam I.: closing war room in 30m if stable, will create postmortem draft template.
Incident Bot: Incident status changed to MONITORING. Tags: customer:cerulean severity:sev2 mitigation:throttle+routing+pool-edit.
Sam I.: (final) Mitigated -> p99 stabilized ~1.2s, p95 0.9s after quota bump and pool edits; leaving monitoring on for 2 hours. Postmortem owner: Jordan P.
Carla CSM: noted, I'll append customer-facing timeline.
Jordan P.: starting postmortem doc now, will ping for reviews.
